event.summary: Interrupted documentation still calls boot-id change its only detector
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 08399d092d20815ced6619c26df2391944ae2b4a. TLDR: internal protocol documentation describes interruption through a changed boot id even though the same variant also represents startup retirement of old terminals. Details: lib.rs:847-859 explicitly describes both reboot and old-server retirement, then calls the changed stored boot id the one detector. The assigned patch changes only the first paragraph; its patch context shows that the one-detector sentence is unchanged, and the old first paragraph already named an update ending an old terminal. This is a pre-existing explanatory inconsistency, not a defect introduced by removing tmux-era descriptions. SPEC_impl.md at this revision, Ending the old private tmux server, states that reload converts launching/running/stopping old-kind agents to interrupted via Transition::TerminalEnded beside reboot conversion. Suggested bucket: other (internal documentation accuracy). Confidence: confirmed from source and patch; no execution. proposed_drop: outside assigned change, because the contradictory explanation and the second route both predate this patch. possible_cover: none; excluded coverage sources not searched. Could-be-highest: false; this wording gives no operational instruction or security/data-loss guidance. No runtime or wire representation change is claimed.

event.summary: Interruption documentation still claims boot-id change is its only detector
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 08399d092d20815ced6619c26df2391944ae2b4a; introduced by dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4 within the pinned range. TLDR: a developer reading the shared protocol contract is told an interrupted session proves a reboot detector ran, although an ordinary update can produce the same status without a reboot. This is misleading internal documentation, with no observed runtime malfunction. Details: at reviewed lib.rs:849-859, the first paragraph correctly includes startup retirement of an old terminal, but lines 855-857 still define Interrupted as 'asked, via the one reboot detector this system has (a changed stored boot id)'. The exclusive base 6e423e30068b62c6cfa276c6d720ee35bb70387a lib.rs:842-852 described only reboot. The full-range -G history identifies dbfc69751215dbf15e1d31d5bed73c3754c4ebc4 as adding the update-ended-terminal route while retaining that definition; its lib.rs patch shows both claims together. Its SPEC_impl.md:2978-2980 says: 'The reload then takes every old-kind row as having no terminal, in any state, without looking its recorded pane id up: one whose agent was launching, running or being stopped is converted to interrupted (`Transition::TerminalEnded`, beside the reboot conversion) unless its launch sentinel makes it an error'. This is a second attribution path, not evidence of a changed boot id. At the assigned cleanup commit, the parent paragraph already has the contradiction, but that is insufficient grounds to drop a range-review finding. Suggested fix: describe interruption as a durable lost-track outcome established by reboot or retirement of an old terminal, without claiming all instances come from a boot-id change. Suggested bucket: other. Confidence: confirmed by source, introducing patch and exact specification contract; no execution. proposed_drop: false; the original proposed drop (pre-existing outside scope) is retracted because the contract change is inside the reviewed range. possible_cover: none; parent owns queue coverage and excluded sources were not read. Could-be-highest: false; the consequence remains inaccurate internal documentation, with no operational instruction or established security/data-loss route. Caveat: the executable retirement behavior is specified and accepted; this finding concerns the explanation only and must not be rendered as a runtime correctness failure.

event.summary: Cached activity does not contradict fresh host-backed status projection
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 08399d092d20815ced6619c26df2391944ae2b4a. TLDR: considered whether the revised status documentation incorrectly promises fresh status while the system retains a cached classification across supervisor restart. No additional documentation defect is established by that cache. Source refutation: service/status.rs:141-252 derives liveness from HostEvidence and combines it with the durable outcome; an observable live terminal selects live_status rather than blindly replaying a stored wire status. status.rs:255-310 reads the current entry's activity cell and returns Unknown for startup_provisional unless Waiting is recognized. Its exact contract states: 'A reloaded terminal has no such fresh launch evidence, so it reports Unknown while the helm retains the preceding cached status.' Thus the supervisor's fresh wire projection and the helm's retained display answer are separate. The documentation at proto/lib.rs:757-763 already says list/rename use fresh terminal liveness plus cached classification, rather than promising fresh screen sampling per reply. Durable LastOutcome::Running is explicitly distinguished from wire status in status.rs:184-189. Suggested bucket: other if there were a wording defect. Confidence: confirmed source distinction; no execution. proposed_drop: source-refuted concern, based on the exact separation quoted above; no claim that all caches are absent or that every unchanged sentence in this old doc is perfect. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: false; this considered concern is internal status-contract wording with no established security or loss-of-work route. Material caveat: the earlier broad last_activity search was clipped and supplies no negative evidence; the bounded classification source supplies the conclusion. No new runtime failure or independent defect is claimed.
